citation: Bhan, S.C., Devrani, A.K., Sinha, V. (2015), An analysis of monthly rainfall and the meteorological conditions associated with cloudburst over the dry region of Leh (Ladakh), India, MAUSAM 66(1), 107-122.

location.name: Leh, Ladakh
location.most_affected_area: Choglamsar, approximately 5 km south of Leh

event.reported_deaths: About 200; another paper section states more than 200 unofficially

leh_observatory.note: Heaviest rain fell south of Leh and was not measured by the observatory.

chronology.event: Convection began over the Tibetan Plateau southeast of Leh
Convection reached Ladakh after northwestward movement and intensification
TRMM rainfall estimates south of Leh were highest during this interval
Very intense convective cloud persisted over the area until about this time
Convection shifted westward and little rain fell afterward
Landslide occurred after the most intense rainfall spell

environment.western_himalaya_winds: Southeasterly winds of 15-20 kt extended to mid-levels
environment.200_hpa: Anticyclone centered near 35N, 78E, with easterly/southeasterly steering

trmm_3b41rt.progression: Rainfall progressed into the affected region from the southeast.

source_notes: The Hindi abstract gives latitude 30.09N, while the paper text gives 34.09N; this record uses 34.09N.
July/August mean rainfall differs across sections: 15.4/15.2 mm in Section 3, 15.1/12.3 mm in Section 6.1, and 12.6/15.0 mm in Table 1; this record uses Table 1.
